binaryFixes.what: Every host adapter rewrote its instruction file (CLAUDE.md, the OpenCode and Codex AGENTS.md, GEMINI.md, copilot-instructions.md, SOUL.md, the Pi SKILL.md) with read_to_string(..).unwrap_or_default() followed by a plain truncating fs::write. Two `squeez init` runs in the same moment: one read the file while the other had it truncated, took it for empty and wrote the squeez block alone. That wiped the owner rules from the OpenCode v2 AGENTS.md on 2026-10-10T01:17Z (16 KB down to 874 B). src/hosts/memory_file.rs now does the read-modify-write for all seven adapters: an existing file that cannot be read is an error, never empty; a result that drops text outside the squeez block is refused; the write is a temp file in the same directory renamed over the target; one writer at a time through an OS lock on the sibling .<name>.squeez-lock (released by the OS when its holder dies); and the file is re-read before the rename and left alone if it changed. Every refusal leaves the file untouched and is logged to %TEMP%/squeez-write-race-guard.log.

binaryFixes.review: 4f89287: redact owner text in refusals, reject ambiguous markers, compare after fsync and before every rename retry, preserve unowned temp collisions, refuse readonly targets, create Unix temps privately and propagate chmod errors. Review proof includes an external writer during rename retry, killed process mid-write, 10 MB BOM/Unicode/CRLF, readonly targets, corrupted markers and literal shell paths. Detected errors fail closed; an uncooperative writer can still race the final compare and rename. Network/sync-provider semantics, ACL/xattr preservation and power-loss durability are not proven. compress-md remains a separate unguarded write path: keep auto_compress_md=false.

overlays.what: Owner OpenCode plugin: on Windows the wrapper follows the OpenCode `shell` config key, not the OS. A PowerShell shell gets powershell.exe -EncodedCommand (upstream wraps with POSIX quoting and squeez wrap runs them in bash) and WSL commands bounded by a taskkill /F /T supervisor that exits 124; a bash shell gets the POSIX form with a forward-slash quoted binary path, and WSL commands are left unwrapped so the host timeout bounds them. On the win32+bash path the wrapped command additionally gets an outside-envelope guard (upstream #261): the inner wrap stays byte-identical, the whole wrap is redirected to a per-call log and backgrounded, and a watchdog at ceiling+15s tree-kills via /proc/<pid>/winpid if squeez overstays — descendants of squeez leak its std handles and hold the harness pipe past every ceiling; kill-switch <tmpdir>/squeez-wrap-guard.OFF, plain-wrap fallback past 7000 chars (MSYS argv truncation, #262). The plugin starts no child process synchronously: inside the OpenCode server the first execSync of a hook call fails at once with a false ETIMEDOUT, which dropped the read/grep budget; it uses existsSync and async execFile (one retry, 60 s cache). Post-execution tracking pipes a JSON payload to `squeez track-result` over stdin with EOF (the observer no-ops on empty stdin — upstream #247); the v2 path subscribes shell.exited for shell completions and session.execution.started (per-session dedupe) for init.

One file, two entry points: server() for v1 and setup(ctx) for v2 — the v2 path registers on ctx.shell/ctx.tool/ctx.event with the wrapper following the shell each create.before event carries (#244), no synchronous spawns (#245/#246), async budget injection with a 60 s cache, the WSL supervisor on PowerShell shells (#239), and the win32+bash outside-envelope guard (#261: per-call log + watchdog tree-kill via /proc/<pid>/winpid at ceiling+15s, kill-switch <tmpdir>/squeez-wrap-guard.OFF, 7000-char plain-wrap fallback for #262). For a non-Portuguese user that block is a standing instruction in another language in every session. This overlay installs the owner's English translation of the 11 buddy scripts and the /buddy command (2026-10-13). Identifiers, behaviour and file formats are unchanged; the duck keeps its name; lib/state.js maps the Portuguese archetype and intensity values persisted in existing state files to the English ones, so an existing duck keeps its identity. Each file records the SHA-256 of the template it was translated from (LF line endings): a file is re-applied only while the installed tag's template is still that one.

omoClaudeHooksOff.why: oh-my-openagent runs Claude Code PreToolUse hooks on OpenCode tool calls and applies updatedInput with output.args = {...} (packages/utils/src/replace-tool-args.ts). OpenCode executes the original args object (session/tools.ts passes { args } and never reads output.args back), so the Claude hook's wrap is dropped and the squeez plugin, which runs after OMO, edits the detached copy: commands ran raw except the ones squeez should-wrap rejects. Under OpenCode the squeez plugin is the wrapper, so squeez's Claude pretooluse.sh is excluded for OMO. OMO matches the pattern against command.split('/').pop(), which for the registered command is pretooluse.sh followed by a double quote. OMO's non-interactive-env hook detached every command containing the word git the same way; that half is OMO ledger fix 17-tool-args-in-place (oh-my-openagent-fix/local-fixes, 2026-10-02), which makes OMO edit the args in place. With it the Claude hook's rewrite would take effect too, but it only emits the POSIX form (wrong for a PowerShell shell) and also compresses Task prompts, so the exclusion stays and the shell-aware plugin is the only wrapper under OpenCode. Remove only with an owner decision on which wrapper should run.
